# mimi-protocol-06 feedback bundle (DRAFT, not sent)

Repo ietf-wg-mimi/mimi-protocol, main 833394a (= -06). Line numbers are editor's-copy .md lines. Every issue ends with:
"Found implementing -06 in mimid, a Rust implementation of MIMI over MLS. Line numbers are from draft-ietf-mimi-protocol.md at 833394a (= -06)."
Before sending: build the edited .md with kramdown-rfc (`make`; not installed here) to confirm xref/aasvg markup.

## PR: "Editorial fixes to -06 from an implementation pass"
These are editorial fixes found while implementing -06 in mimid, a Rust implementation of MIMI over MLS. None changes bytes on the wire; technical items are separate issues (#A-#I).
- §3 examples: `clubhousee`, missing `/r/` in §3.6 paths, `/submit` -> `/submitMessage` (diagram labels unchanged).
- §3.1: canAddUser/canRemoveUser/canSetUserRole are not in room-policy-04; replaced with canAddParticipant/canRemoveParticipant/canChangeUserRole; "permisions".
- §5.1 directory JSON: `update{roomId}` -> `update/{roomId}`; missing `:` after "proxyDownload"; consent placeholders use {targetDomain}/{requesterDomain} matching §5.7.
- Presentation language: `;` -> `,` in KeyMaterialUserCode/KeyMaterialClientCode; missing `};` closing the HandshakeBundle select; missing `;` in GroupInfoOption, UpdateRoomResponse, ParticipantListUpdate and the §6.1 structs; IdentifierURI -> IdentifierUri; RoomId -> IdentifierUri; string -> UTF8String (§7.6); optional Frank -> optional<Frank>; select(type) -> select(searchType); opaque signature_public_key -> opaque signature_public_key<V>; missing `,` in the SignWithLabel call.
- SubmitMessageResponse: `case success` vs SubmitResponseCode accepted(0); select arm and prose now say `accepted` (bytes unchanged).
- Typos: ExternerSender, groupInfoPublcKey, UpdatedResponseCode, requestContent, UpdateRequest in submitMessage semantics; "Grubs" -> "Grubbs"; mimi://b.example/b/bob -> /u/bob.
- Broken xref `{Section 6.2 of !I-D.ietf-mls-extensions}` -> `{{...}}`.
- Stale draft names: I-D.barnes-mimi-arch -> I-D.ietf-mimi-arch; I-D.mahy-mls-ratchet-tree-options -> I-D.ietf-mls-ratchet-tree-options.
- §10: mls-extensions puts MLS Component Types in §7.5, not 7.6. 0x0021 registered as franking_signature_key but §5.4.1 calls the component franking_agent (franking_signature_key is a field in FrankingAgentData); renamed, same value and anchor. Happy to split this into its own PR.
Diff: see "Editorial diff" at the end (60+/59-).

## Issue #A: AppSync and AppDataUpdate both name the room-state proposal
-06 uses two mechanisms for one operation. §2 (L214) "using the MLS AppSync proposal type ... {{!I-D.barnes-mls-appsync}}"; §4.2 (L631-635) "encapsulated in an AppSync proposal"; §5.3 (L952-954) "an `AppSync` proposal type with the `applicationId` of `mimiParticipantList` or `mimiRoomPolicy`". §4.3.2 (L703-705) and §7.5 (L2300) use mls-extensions AppDataUpdate. draft-barnes-mls-appsync-01 defines ApplicationData/ApplicationDataUpdate, neither called AppSync; applicationId, mimiParticipantList and mimiRoomPolicy exist in no current document. Implementers following the reference build different proposals from those following §4.3.2.
mimid reads every AppSync as AppDataUpdate (0x0008), mapping mimiParticipantList -> participant_list (0x0022) and mimiRoomPolicy -> the room-policy-04 §10.1 components (decision mimid-1wgh.4.16).
Proposed fix: AppDataUpdate throughout (§2, §3 figures, §4.2, §5.3); name participant_list and the room-policy components; drop the barnes-mls-appsync reference.

## Issue #B: frank_aad framing under mls-extensions-10 Safe AAD
-06 cites mls-extensions-09 (editor's-copy citation is unversioned, so -10 on rebuild). -09 §4.9: "the 'safe' AAD items MUST come before any non-safe data"; -10 §4.9: "the entire authenticated_data field is framed as a SafeAAD struct". §5.4.1 (L1170, L1246-1247) puts franking_tag in the frank_aad component but does not say whether franking rooms MUST carry safe_aad (listing 0x0020) in the GroupContext, nor what the hub does when AAD is not a valid SafeAAD or lacks 0x0020. A -09 sender may append non-safe bytes a -10 receiver rejects.
mimid follows -10 (decision mimid-1wgh.4.17).
Proposed fix: cite -10; franking requires safe_aad in the GroupContext listing frank_aad; franking_tag is the aad_item_data of the 0x0020 item; define hub behaviour when absent/malformed.

## Issue #C: `select (protocol)` with no protocol field in scope
ClientKeyMaterial (L878) select (protocol) with no protocol field; UpdateRequest (L1009) select (room.protocol); FanoutMessage (L1408) select (protocol); GroupInfoResponseTBS/GroupInfoResponse (L1579-1582, L1591-1596) declare `Protocol version;` then select (protocol). One implementation will put a Protocol octet on the wire and another won't; every message then fails to parse.
mimid: no protocol octet in UpdateRequest/FanoutMessage; protocol from context (mls10 only); `version` treated as the Protocol field (decision mimid-1wgh.5.23).
Proposed fix: add `Protocol protocol;` where needed and rename version -> protocol, or say explicitly the value comes from the enclosing struct/room. Related: #D, #52.

## Issue #D: FanoutMessage selects content types on wire_format
L1414-1428: select (message.wire_format) with arms application, welcome, proposal, commit. Only mls_welcome is a WireFormat (RFC 9420 §6); the others are ContentType values. Per L1411-1412 a proposal/commit can be PublicMessage or SemiPrivateMessage, so the arm can't be chosen from wire_format alone (SemiPrivateMessage carries content_type in the clear).
mimid: welcome -> mls_welcome; application -> PrivateMessage; proposal/commit -> a PublicMessage's content_type (decision mimid-1wgh.5.24).
Proposed fix: select on wire_format, then on content_type for public/semi-private. Related: #C.

## Issue #E: GroupInfo request/response signature and encryption inputs are ambiguous
1. joiningCode is `optional opaque joiningCode<V>` in GroupInfoRequestTBS (L1524) but `opaque joiningCode<V>` in GroupInfoRequest (L1536); a verifier can't rebuild the TBS; `optional opaque` is not RFC 9420 syntax.
2. GroupInfoResponseTBS (L1578-1588) lacks the select (status) GroupInfoResponse (L1594) has; TBS for non-success is undefined.
3. EncryptWithLabel context is `room_id` (L1575): raw URI bytes or length-prefixed opaque room_id<V>?
Each divergent reading breaks the signature or decryption.
mimid: joiningCode optional in both per L1504-1505 (decision mimid-1wgh.5.22); TBS only on success (mimid-1wgh.5.26); raw URI bytes as context (mimid-1wgh.5.30).
Proposed fix: one joiningCode encoding in both; mirror the status select in the TBS; state the exact context bytes.

## Issue #F: Receivers have no defined source for room_uri when verifying a frank
§5.4.1.3 (L1317-1332): the receiver rebuilds ServerFrankingContext incl. room_uri and checks the content's room_uri "matches the room ID in the received message". §5.4.1.2 (L1299-1301) says the hub fans out "the room URI", but neither FanoutMessage (L1404-1431) nor Frank (L1117-1121) has a room URI field. Receivers taking room_uri from different places compute different TBS bytes.
mimid takes it from the /notify/{roomId} path (decision mimid-1wgh.5.15).
Proposed fix: state it comes from the /notify path and the follower passes it to the client, or carry it in FanoutMessage.

## Issue #G: KeyMaterialRequest.roomId required on the wire but conditional in prose
L780-782: "When the request is being made in the context of adding the target user to a room, the request MUST include the room ID". KeyMaterialRequest and its TBS (L803, L820) have a bare `IdentifierUri roomId;` and nothing says what to send outside a room. ConsentEntry (L1685) uses optional for the same idea.
mimid treats a zero-length URI as absent (decision mimid-1wgh.5.27).
Proposed fix: `optional<IdentifierUri> roomId;` in both (wire change), or state zero length means absent. Related: #149 touches the same struct.

## Issue #H: §10 lacks the well-known URI and media type registrations
§5.1 (L733-737) uses /.well-known/mimi-protocol-directory but §10 registers only the four MLS components. RFC 8615 §3.1 requires registering well-known URIs. No Content-Type is defined for the binary bodies.
mimid recorded the gap (decision mimid-1wgh.5.33).
Proposed fix: register the well-known URI; define a media type for TLS-encoded bodies or state which to use.

## Issue #I: Endpoint path prefix and placeholder expansion are unspecified
1. The §5.1 directory (L743-759) uses /v1/...; §5.2-5.10 (L770, L949, L1081, L1401, L1497, L1644, L1751, L1895, L2009) have no prefix.
2. Nothing says whether directory values are RFC 6570 templates or how {roomId}, {targetUser}, {downloadUrl} are filled; L778 says only "with any necessary percent-encoding". The §3 flows strip the scheme (/notify/a.example/r/clubhouse); RFC 6570 simple expansion of mimi://a.example/r/clubhouse gives mimi%3A%2F%2Fa.example%2Fr%2Fclubhouse. Different request targets; a peer that guesses differently gets a 404.
mimid: /v1 prefix (decision mimid-1wgh.5.37); RFC 6570 level-1 simple expansion of the full URI (mimid-1wgh.5.38, mimid-1wgh.5.18).
Proposed fix: directory values are RFC 6570 level-1 templates whose variables are full URIs; §5.x paths illustrative; update §3 examples. Related: #52 doesn't cover this.

## mimi@ietf.org message
Subject: draft-ietf-mimi-protocol-06: implementation feedback (1 PR, 9 issues)

I filed one editorial PR and nine issues against draft-ietf-mimi-protocol-06, found while implementing it in mimid, a Rust implementation of MIMI over MLS.

The PR changes no bytes on the wire: typos, presentation-language syntax, stale draft names, the §3 example paths, and the §10 component name. [PR link]

The issues each have interop impact; two implementations reading -06 differently will fail to talk:
- AppSync vs AppDataUpdate [#A]
- frank_aad framing under mls-extensions-10 Safe AAD [#B]
- `select (protocol)` with no protocol field [#C]
- FanoutMessage selecting content types on wire_format [#D]
- GroupInfo signature and encryption inputs [#E]
- where receivers get room_uri for frank verification [#F]
- optional roomId in KeyMaterialRequest [#G]
- missing well-known and media-type registrations [#H]
- endpoint prefix and placeholder expansion [#I]

Each issue says what mimid chose, so there is one concrete reading to compare against.

-06 expires 27 October. A -07 that resolves #C, #D and #E would let independent implementations interoperate on the wire.

I can offer mimid for an RFC 7942 Implementation Status section, if the editors want one.

Mark Atwood
